title: Cross-environment promotion guardrails for model promotions and experiments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: build a unified promotion guardrail service that coordinates canary rollouts, A/B experiments, shadow traffic, and auto-rollback across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments while preserving environment-specific constraints and configuration parity.

Background: teams need to promote model versions from staging to production with minimal risk. Hosted deployments have flexible routing and burst capacity. Dedicated deployments guarantee reserved throughput but cannot always accept arbitrary shadow traffic due to capacity isolation. Private (VPC/on-prem) customers impose network, KMS, and operator approval constraints. Current rollout logic lives in multiple places and produces drift in behavior across environments.

Scope: implement a coordination layer and translation rules that:
- Provide a single API for promotion orchestration (promote:/release, experiment:/start, traffic:/shadow) that maps to environment-specific primitives.
- Enforce safety checks before ramping traffic (capacity check, KV-cache warmup, model size/quantization compatibility, region/cost limits).
- Support staged ramps for canaries and A/B traffic with flexible schedules and percentile-based SLO evaluation windows.
- Enable non-invasive shadowing in Hosted; in Dedicated run synthetic shadow runners with rate limits; in Private surface a templated playbook for ops-run shadowing if automated shadowing is disabled.
- Define deterministic auto-rollback triggers based on latency P99, error-rate, hallucination/quality regression signals from eval sets, and token-cost anomalies.
- Preserve auditability and compliance: log decisions, require optional human approval for Private, and integrate with KMS/HSM and SSO for promotion authorization.

Acceptance criteria:
- Single promotion API that returns a promotion plan preview showing environment differences.
- Automated pre-checks succeed/fail with actionable errors for all three environments.
- Canary/A-B ramps can be configured with percent, duration, metric windows, and success thresholds.
- Auto-rollback rules configurable per project and per environment; rollout halts when thresholds breached and a rollback job is created.
- Telemetry: per-promotion dashboards with traffic split, cost delta, and quality regressions; links to logs and candidate PR for rollouts.
- Private deployments: if auto-apply is disabled, promotion plan includes a markdown playbook and a dry-run manifest that operators can apply via their control plane.

Design decisions / trade-offs considered:
- Centralized coordination vs per-environment agents: chosen hybrid. Central coordination produces a canonical plan and pre-checks. Lightweight environment agents execute translated plans. This reduces central blast radius while keeping parity.
- Shadowing semantics: fully automated shadowing in Hosted is safest for continuous QA. For Dedicated, automated shadowing is allowed but rate-limited. For Private, we prefer operator-driven shadow runs to respect customer policy.
- Rollback aggressiveness: default thresholds conservative (short windows for latency spikes, longer windows for quality regressions) to avoid noisy rollbacks. Teams can tune per-project.
- KV-cache warmup: warmup performed on canary nodes with synthetic prefix caching. This adds cost but avoids cold-start regressions.

Delivery plan:
1) Spec and canonical plan schema (this ticket) — complete
2) Central Promotion Service MVP: plan generation, pre-checks, preview API — in progress
3) Environment agents: Hosted executor, Dedicated executor (capacity-aware), Private dry-run generator + operator playbook — next sprint
4) Telemetry dashboards and auto-rollback worker with configurable policies — follow-up

Testing / QA:
- Integration tests that simulate Hosted/Dedicated/Private executors with a matrix of constraints (quota, network denial, KMS unavailable).
- Canary simulation harness that injects latency and quality regressions to validate rollback behavior.
- Manual runbook verification for Private deployments and operator acceptance tests.

Acceptance signal for launch: two pilot customers (one Hosted-first SaaS, one Dedicated) run promotions end-to-end with no manual rollback required in > 90% of trials and clear operator steps for Private.
